comparator.name: Health and Life Sciences (Gezondheid en Leven)
comparator.sourceNotes: For Fall 2026 entrants, the adopted 2026–2027 regulations establish ten compulsory 6 EC first-year courses and at least 30 EC open study in the first semester of Year 3. The curriculum revision removes the old BMW/DGZ/KW specialisations. Its Year 2 has six compulsory courses and four choice slots, including Genomics versus Qualitative Research and Anatomy/Physiology 2 versus System Transformation. It describes biomedical or societal research in Year 3, preparatory methods for the societal project and a final Science Communication course, but supplies no applicable future component-credit table. Old 18/24 EC thesis weights and outgoing specialisation tables cannot be imported. Lab safety is required before the Biochemistry practical; its grade also requires the Dutch diagnostic pass or completed refresher. Toxicology/Epidemiology requires completion of Year-1 study/career guidance. These noncredit conditions are separate from 180 EC. BSA normally requires 42 first-year EC. Attendance rules follow course manuals. Open study needs approval except stated minor exemptions, nonoverlap, at least 12 EC level 300 and at most 6 EC level 100; subjects in the degree field must be level 300. Listed minors remain conditional on entrance requirements and nonoverlap. Optional honours are excluded.

components.note: OER article 12.1 establishes at least 30 EC; the new-curriculum explanation places the minor in periods 1–3. This records the 30-EC minimum only, without selecting a minor.

exception.reason: A complete Fall 2026 entrant pathway remains unresolved: the applicable Year-2 credit allocation and choice rules, and Year-3 research, preparatory-methods and science-communication credits are not established by the current sources. Only 90 EC can be retained with explicit weights. The sources were successfully retrieved and inspected; this is a documented cohort-information gap, not transient source inaccessibility or a UCR no-match conclusion.

audience.programmeDescription: VU Gezondheid en Leven studies health from molecules and the human body to behavior, society, healthcare systems and the environment. Fall 2026 entrants combine biomedical and societal study without the former graduation specialisations.
audience.comparisonExplanation: A complete comparison is awaiting verified curriculum information for Fall 2026 entrants. The confirmed subset below contains 60 EC of first-year study and a 30 EC open-study semester. Credits and choice rules for the remaining curriculum are unresolved, so no UCR alternative is presented. This does not establish that a UCR response is impossible.

curriculum.limitation: Verified subset: 90 of 180 EC. The remaining new-cohort course credits, Year-2 choice rules and final research/communication requirements need confirmation. The older specialisation tables do not supply those facts. Lab safety precedes the Biochemistry practical; the Dutch language requirement gates its grade. First-year study/career guidance also gates Toxicology and Epidemiology.
